verses.text: The box of the LORD had been in Philistine land for seven months.
Then the Philistines called for their priests and fortune-tellers and asked, "What shall we do with the box of the LORD? Tell us how we should send it back to its place."

They answered, "If you send back the box of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty. Be sure to send a guilt offering to him. Then you will be healed, and you will understand why his hand has not turned away from you."

The Philistines asked, "What guilt offering should we send to him?" They replied, "Five gold swellings and five gold rats, one for each of the five Philistine rulers, because the same plague has struck both you and your rulers.
Make models of the swellings and of the rats that are ruining the country, and give honour to the God of Israel. Perhaps he will lift his hand from you and your gods and your land.
Why make your hearts stubborn as the Egyptians and Pharaoh did? When God had dealt harshly with them, did they not let the Israelites go on their way?
Now then, get a new cart ready, with two cows that have had calves and have never been yoked. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves away and pen them up.
Take the box of the LORD and put it on the cart. Beside it, put a chest with the gold objects you are sending him as a guilt offering. Then send it on its way,

and watch. If it goes up toward its own land, toward Beth Shemesh, then the LORD has brought this great disaster on us. But if it does not, then we will know that it was not his hand that struck us. It just happened by chance."
So they did this. They took two cows that had calves, hitched them to the cart and penned up their calves.
They put the box of the LORD on the cart, together with the chest holding the gold rats and the models of the swellings.

Then the cows went straight up toward Beth Shemesh. They kept on the road, mooing all the way, and did not turn to the right or to the left. The rulers of the Philistines followed them as far as the border of Beth Shemesh.
The people of Beth Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the box, they were overjoyed.
The cart came to the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh and stopped there beside a large rock. The people chopped up the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

The Levites took down the box of the LORD, together with the chest holding the gold objects, and placed them on the large rock. That day the people of Beth Shemesh offered burnt offerings and made sacrifices to the LORD.
The five rulers of the Philistines saw all this and then went back to Ekron that same day.
These are the gold swellings the Philistines sent as a guilt offering to the LORD: one each for Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron.

And the number of the gold rats matched the number of Philistine towns belonging to the five rulers, both the walled cities and the country villages. The large rock where they set the box of the LORD is still a witness to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh.

But God struck down some of the men of Beth Shemesh because they looked into the box of the LORD. He struck down fifty thousand and seventy of them. The people mourned because of the terrible blow the LORD had dealt them.
The people of Beth Shemesh asked, "Who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God? Where can the box go from here?"
Then they sent messengers to the people of Kiriath Jearim, saying, "The Philistines have sent back the box of the LORD. Come down and take it up to your town."
